title: Bolt.new
summary: An AI builder with a documented JavaScript web-app path.

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: JavaScript web apps; mobile path uses Expo

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: The policy's general rule says eligible Bolt AI content may be used for model development and de-identified dataset licensing unless opted out, starting no earlier than 2026-10-07 or a later account Terms date. Exception: Forge content created or generated from 2026-09-14 may be eligible under separate affirmative consent. Regional and account exclusions apply.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Official documentation provides a GitHub version-control integration.

sections.heading: Check the technology fit
paragraphs: The official introduction describes JavaScript web frameworks and an Expo path for mobile applications. Verify the dependencies and backend requirements of your intended project instead of interpreting that scope as support for every language.

sections.heading: Review the exported project
paragraphs: Use the documented GitHub integration and test a clean checkout. Confirm environment variables, database access and the deployment procedure separately. Token allowances should be evaluated against observed work, not converted into an invented number of finished features.

pros.text: Bolt documents full-stack web apps built with JavaScript-based frameworks and a separate Expo route for mobile apps.
The product documentation describes GitHub version control alongside databases and hosting in Bolt Cloud.

cons.text: The documented full-stack web-app scope is JavaScript-based; confirm support before choosing a project built around another language or framework.
GitHub sync should be rehearsed as a handoff; the integration docs describe repository sync rather than an in-product merge workflow.

The published privacy policy describes prospective model-development and dataset-licensing uses for eligible Bolt AI content. Effective dates, Forge consent, account exclusions and opt-out controls must be checked against the account; none were inspected.

faqs.question: Can Bolt start from an existing repository?
faqs.answer: The official introduction describes importing an existing GitHub repository. Test a clean checkout and its external services before relying on the handoff.

faqs.question: Does its documented web-app path cover every language?
faqs.answer: The documentation describes JavaScript-based web frameworks, so verify the exact framework and dependencies for your project.

faqs.question: Can Bolt use project content to develop AI models?
faqs.answer: The policy says eligible Bolt AI inputs, outputs, related interaction data and project content processed by Bolt AI features may be used for model development and de-identified dataset licensing unless opted out. For non-Forge content, use starts no earlier than 2026-10-07 or a later account Terms date. Forge content created or generated from 2026-09-14 may be eligible under separate affirmative consent. It excludes EEA, UK and Switzerland accounts and organization-managed accounts unless an administrator enables the uses. The policy was checked on 2026-09-28; this account's effective date, region, agreement and settings were not checked.

verdict: Shortlist Bolt for a prototype that fits its documented technology scope. Validate the export and deployment steps before choosing a paid tier.
notFor: Projects assuming every backend language is supported
migration: Rehearse the GitHub handoff, then build from a clean checkout. Inventory database, hosting and secret configuration separately from the code.
gaps: Verify the account's applicable Terms effective date, region, organization-managed status, model-development opt-out and any Bolt Forge consent; no account settings or agreement were inspected.
